verdict.reasoning: Patient reports low energy for a few weeks and then clarifies duration as about two months: 'over the last few weeks or so...'; later, 'More like two months, I would say. Yeah.'
Difficulty waking: 'I don't really feel like getting up in the morning is really difficult'; insomnia: 'it's more like I'm just having trouble sleeping at all.'
'I'm not eating very much at the moment' directly supports decreased appetite.

'Finding it really hard to. Quite difficult to keep focusing. I would say... just not focused.' and GP summary 'difficulty focusing, quite distracted' support decreased concentration and being easily distracted.
Patient acknowledges low mood: 'Actually now you mentioned it, like my mood is lower recently'; GP reiterates 'your mood has been slightly lower.'

Patient: 'my mood is lower recently and so I Like my sex drive has kind of decreased over the past few months as well'; later 'just over the last few months, just been disinterested.' This supports decreased libido and disinterest in sex.
Patient: 'when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe. So I have some kind of like shortness of breath when doing sports.' This is exertional dyspnea.
Patient links onset to new job: 'I also started a new job slightly recently. It might have even coincided with that job a couple of months ago.' and duration 'More like two months, I would say.'
On suicidality: 'Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or harming anyone else?' / Patient: 'No, no, no, not really.' This supports denial of suicidal and homicidal ideation.
Patient: 'in the past I have a history of hypothyroidism... Hypo Hypo.' GP confirms: 'Okay. Hypothyroid.'
Patient: 'I have a drug history of thyroxine...'; when asked 'Do you continue to take thyroxine now?' Patient: 'Yes.' and GP: 'So you're taking thyroxine at the moment?'; Doctor: 'Yes.'
On allergies: 'Are you allergic to any medications?' / Patient: 'No, I have no medication. Allergies?' / GP: 'No allergies.'
Patient: 'my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago.'
GP: 'And your mother is as well?' / Patient: 'Yeah, she's fine.' This supports that his mother is well.
When asked about relationship: 'Yeah, I'm married. I've been for many years.'
Symptom/job timing: 'I also started a new job slightly recently... that job a couple of months ago.' GP: 'When did you start your new job? Two months ago, did you say?' / Patient: 'Yeah.'

This is a tele-consultation and the clinician says they would like to see him in person for an examination, implying no exam/vitals have yet been done: 'I would like to probably see you in person and do an examination and also we probably like to do some blood tests as well.' No vitals/physical findings are documented in the transcript.

All components are in transcript: fatigue/low energy ('I don't have much energy at all during the day'), insomnia ('trouble sleeping at all'), decreased appetite ('I'm not eating very much at the moment'), low mood ('my mood is lower recently'), decreased libido ('my sex drive has kind of decreased'), exertional SOB ('shortness of breath when doing sports'), and duration about 2 months ('More like two months, I would say.').

Transcript confirms hypothyroidism on thyroxine but there is no explicit discussion of ruling out suboptimal control: only 'I have a history of hypothyroidism...'; 'So you're taking thyroxine at the moment?' There is no statement about needing to rule out suboptimal thyroid control.

Depressive symptoms: low mood, low energy, decreased appetite, decreased libido, poor concentration are described. No suicidal ideation: 'Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or harming anyone else?' / 'No, no, no, not really.' and GP: 'I'm glad you're, you know, although you have a low mood, you're not feeling suicidal, just to confirm that.'

Plan: 'I would like to probably see you in person and do an examination... Do you think it'd be possible to... book an appointment in the next few days with your GP... and then we could... do an examination.'

Plan for blood tests is explicit but specific panels are not named. GP: 'we probably like to do some blood tests as well... do some investigations, really, to see what's going on.' Thyroid function tests and FBC are not specified, so naming them is an added detail.
While suicidality is assessed and noted as absent, there is no explicit plan to 'monitor the patient's mood and provide emergency advice if suicidal ideation develops' in the transcript.

The transcript mentions arranging an in-person GP appointment and doing tests but does not state a specific follow-up plan after blood test results: 'we could... do some investigations... to see what's going on.' No explicit follow-up timing/arrangement is discussed.
As above, there is no explicit agreement that the patient 'will have follow-up after test results and assessment'; only that they should book an appointment for examination and investigations.
